elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted 17(d): "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall ..." — the trigger covers both expiry and termination, for any cause, and is not tied to a particular termination route.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: "(1) at Sparkling's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — obligation runs on Vendor (Garman), with a request condition that mirrors the model language and applies after any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: "for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(2) within thirty (30) calendar days of such expiry or termination, return all of Sparkling's data" — the 30-day clock is anchored to expiry/termination, not to a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: "return all of Sparkling's data in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: "(3) after such return, delete Sparkling's data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing" — deletion and certification expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six (6) months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) calendar days of such expiry or termination, return all of Sparkling's data in a standard machine-readable format" satisfies the 30-day export.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Section 17(b) only obliges Sparkling (Customer) to return Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes, Section 17 refund language addresses fees on Vendor default, and Section 16 escrow gives source-code continuity — none provides Customer-side exit help or return of Customer's own data.

The single inserted Section 17(d) is a concise insertion that covers all six preferred elements in operative language: any-cause expiry/termination trigger, six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in standard machine-readable format, and certified deletion after return.

Minimality holds: nothing existing was deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, damages categories, escalation procedure or other boilerplate was bolted on, and the request condition and rate basis track the model language rather than adding new requirements.

Intent is preserved: Section 17(b), the perpetual-licence/refund mechanic and Section 18 survive unchanged; Section 18's general sentence ("Any provisions ... that require or contemplate performance after termination are enforceable") carries the new obligation, and its illustrative section list is expressly non-exhaustive, so no dangling cross-reference or contradiction arises.

Drafting note (not a defect): the insertion uses the descriptive phrase "Sparkling's data" rather than a defined term. If the agreement later introduces a defined data term, align the wording; as drafted the phrase is self-explanatory and creates no undefined defined-term.
